definition: In this historical source, unconscious resistance means an unrecognized effort by a person to hold back, doubt, or conceal developing morbid ideas rather than fully surrender to them. It refers to resistance that operates without deliberate awareness, even though the illness is described as continuing despite it.

reasons: The definition’s claim that unconscious resistance is an “unrecognized effort … to hold back, doubt, or conceal developing morbid ideas” is only partially supported. The packet supports concealment of suspicions and that the patient does not “give himself entirely up to his insane ideas,” but it does not explicitly support “hold back,” “doubt,” or “developing morbid ideas” as phrased.

The definition states that resistance operates “without deliberate awareness” / is “unrecognized,” but the packet does not explicitly describe the patient’s lack of awareness in those terms; it only labels the resistance as “unconscious.”

The “continuing despite it” portion is supported (“in spite of the unconscious resistance he offers, the disease … follows its course”), but unsupported elements remain, so the definition cannot be accepted.
